events.description: Make the Ware Center for the Arts part of your Lancaster City First Friday route! At 7 pm in the lobby, join the members of Heartland Marimba as they reveal all the insider goodies about their fascinating instrument. Listen, touch, and learn as you explore the science of its acoustics, trace its history from Africa to Central America to the classical music stage, and hear the untold stories of the marimba’s Pennsylvania roots—including tales of the “godfather” of classical marimba, Clair Musser, who hailed from Manheim, PA. events.title: Body Talks
events.description: Body Talks is a Saturday morning gathering for women who want to have honest conversations about bodies, confidence, aging, sex, visibility and what it actually feels like to live in a body that is changing. The body you have vs. the body you were told you should have. When did having a body become so much effing work? The weight. The clothes. The cellulite. The aging. The comparison. The constant feeling that we should be doing something to make our bodies better. And somewhere along the way, a lot of us stopped actually living in our bodies and started managing them instead. So let's talk about it. And yes, there will be mimosas. What to expect: 🥂 Mimosas (N/A option too!) 💃 A little movement 💬 Honest conversation 👯‍♀️ A chance to meet other women ✨ A welcoming space to show up exactly as you are And what you won't find: No therapy. No awkward icebreakers. No pressure to “fix” yourself. Think brunch with women who are willing to talk about real sh*t. We'll start with a conversation about the body we have versus the body we were taught we should have, explore some of the ridiculous expectations women carry around their bodies and get a little more connected to the bodies we're actually living in through simple body movement prompts. You don't need to be confident. You don't need to love your body. You don't need to know anyone else coming. Where comfy clothes that you can move around in. And a yoga mat (if you have one.) Limited to 12 women. $35 before 10/24 $40 after 10/24 Come exactly as you are. No body transformation required.

events.title: SparkDate: Court is in Session
events.description: A Lancaster hidden gem tucked down its own side street — the kind of easy, unpretentious neighborhood bar where there's no dress code and no scene, just a comfortable room where people actually talk. Nobody has to perform here, which is exactly what you want on a night like this. Pair that with a room full of singles who showed up on purpose, and you've got a Tuesday night that actually goes somewhere. How the night works. You check in with a host and get a name tag — there's nothing to download and no profile to fill out at the door. The evening runs in three movements. First, you're seated at a small table with a game to play — that's the icebreaker, so nobody has to invent an opening line cold — and the men move one table along each round, which means every round is a genuinely new set of people. Then the structure drops away and it's open mingling: go where you want, talk to whoever you want, for as long as it's working. By that point you've already met most of the room, so nobody is starting cold — which is the part a bar full of strangers never gets right. Last, one-on-ones with the people you haven't already sat with. Near the end you privately note anyone you'd like to see again; it takes under a minute and nobody else sees it. If someone noted you back, that's a match, and you both get it that night rather than after some review period. Why it's built this way. Everyone in the room came out on purpose on a Tuesday night. That's a filter no dating app has. Open-Captioned performances provide patrons with live text presentation of onstage dialogue on a LED screen situated in a box to the right side of the stage. The captions seen on the LED screen may be read from most seats in the theatre, though many prefer seats in the Parquet or Orchestra sections for the best view. An experienced captioner scrolls text in sync with the actors’ spoken word. Tickets can be reserved at the box office or online. events.title: Beethoven 9 with the Lancaster Symphony Orchestra & Choir
events.description: The Lancaster Symphony Orchestra & Choir crowns its 80th Anniversary Season with one of music's most monumental achievements: Beethoven's Ninth Symphony. This historic finale features the regional premiere of Jeffrey Nytch's powerful Hunger Stones—a contemplative work inspired by ancient climate warnings carved into European riverbeds—and Brahms' joyful Academic Festival Overture, a rousing potpourri of student songs. The evening culminates with Beethoven's revolutionary Ninth Symphony, uniting orchestra, chorus, and vocal soloists in the transcendent "Ode to Joy"—a triumphant celebration of humanity's highest aspirations. From ancient warnings to eternal joy, this season finale honors 80 years of the Lancaster Symphony Orchestra bringing music and community together. events.title: Phantom Accessibility Show at the Fulton
events.description: ASL Interpretation: Certified interpreters for select performances provide American Sign Language interpretation. To access special reserved seating, complete an Accessibility Ticket Reservation Form. If you need to cancel your reservation, contact access@thefulton.org so that we may extend an offer to wait-listed patrons. The Pay-What-You-Want program is available for patrons who are deaf or hard of hearing at all ASL interpreted performances. Audio Description is a carefully timed narration of the onstage visual elements in the performance, including the action, costumes, and scenery. Program notes via headset are available 10 to 15 minutes before show time, and a touch tour may be available 1 hour before the show depending on the production (details will be sent via e-mail if a touch tour is available and a separate no-cost reservation will be required). The simultaneous description is broadcast live via an inconspicuous FM receiver. Patrons may choose a single earpiece, dual headset, or a neck loop (for patrons using a hearing aid with a “T” switch), and the device may be used in any seat in the theatre. Patrons may pick up their receiver and headset, free-of-charge, at Audience Services, located in the coat room on the right side of the main lobby. Open-Captioned performances provide patrons with live text presentation of onstage dialogue on a LED screen situated in a box to the right side of the stage. The captions seen on the LED screen may be read from most seats in the theatre, though many prefer seats in the Parquet or Orchestra sections for the best view. An experienced captioner scrolls text in sync with the actors’ spoken word. Tickets can be reserved at the box office or online. The Pay-What-You-Want program is available for patrons who are deaf or hard of hearing at the open captioned performances listed below. Please fill out the Accessibility Ticket Reservation Form for the Pay-What-You-Want rate for the performances listed below.
